title: Ego and the Name can't share a room
hookLine: Guru Amar Das wrote many hymns on ego, the Word and the mind
carry: ego and the name can't share one room
tomorrow: You are the form of light

lines: A LATE ARRIVAL, A LONG SERVICE.
cards: A page of the Guru Granth Sahib, and above the hymn, a small heading: Mahala three. The signature in the verses is still Nanak. But the voice has changed.
Sikh tradition remembers Guru Amar Das as a man who came to the Guru late in life, carried water before dawn for years, and became Guru as an old man. Guru Angad spoke in short verses.
His successor's hymns keep circling three things: ego, the Word, and the mind.

teach.h: TWO CANNOT LIVE IN ONE PLACE.
teach.b: Start with one line from the Var in Raga Vadhans, paraphrased: ego and the Name are opposed to each other; the two do not dwell in one place. That's the whole map in a sentence.
Ego, in Punjabi haumai, is the feeling of I, I, mine, mine, the self at the center of every room. The Name, and the Word that carries it, is the Guru's teaching living in you.

teach.h: HE TALKS TO THE MIND, NOT AGAINST IT.
teach.b: And the place where they can't live together is the mind, the man.

teach.h: THE WORD TAKES UP THE ROOM.
teach.b: Picture a small house with room for one guest: ego has the room, or the Word has it. Notice what he doesn't say. He doesn't call the mind bad.

He talks to it, again and again, the way you'd talk to someone you love who keeps wandering off. In the Anand, his song of bliss, he says, again paraphrased: O my mind, stay always with the Lord. That's not a scolding.
It's a call home. And the way home, in his hymns, is the Word. Not willpower, not cleverness: the Guru's Word, heard, sung and remembered, until it takes the room where ego used to sprawl.
Some readers hear in this a man who served a long time before anyone called him Guru. He knows how ego dresses up, even inside service, and that the mind doesn't settle because you tell it once.
So he says it more than once, patiently.
That patience is the old Guru's voice.

how: Sikhs hear Guru Amar Das's hymns, headed Mahala 3, in kirtan at the gurdwara and in daily prayer: the Anand Sahib, which he composed, is part of the daily banis and is sung at the close of gatherings.

games.q: what does “the old guru's voice” mean?
o: the voice of Guru Nanak in his last years, near the end
an elder who reads the hymns aloud at a gurdwara
Guru Amar Das's patient hymns on ego, the Word and the mind

games.q: the three things his hymns circle: tap the pairs.
p: the Guru's teaching that brings you home
the mind, spoken to like a wanderer

s: in his hymns, ego and the Name can share the mind comfortably
his line says the two are opposed and do not dwell in one place.
Guru Amar Das scolds the mind as something bad
he talks to it like a loved one who wanders: O my mind, stay with the Lord.
his hymns are signed Nanak, with the heading Mahala three
the signature stays the same; the heading shows whose voice it is.

games.q: the mind keeps wandering after things, and ego fills every room. in his hymns, what brings the mind home?
o: the Guru's Word, heard and remembered.
leaving the house for the forest.
games.why: in his hymns it's the Word: heard, sung and remembered until it takes the room where ego sprawled.

practice: Read one of his hymns slowly, once: anything headed Mahala three in a gutka or Gurbani app, the first verse of the Anand, or just today's line, ego and the Name don't dwell in one place.
Then sit with it and ask which of the three it spoke to, ego, the Word or the mind, and keep that one in view without needing to explain it. If you pray, say Waheguru quietly on each breath out.

wordCard.voice: The old Guru's voice: Guru Amar Das, under the heading Mahala three, patient and plain, speaking again and again of ego, the Word, and the mind. Today's word.

orig.note: ego, the sense of I and mine; one of the subjects his hymns return to again and again.

carryVoice: Your line: ego and the Name can't share one room. Guru Amar Das calls the mind home through the Word. See you tomorrow.

sources.ref: Guru Granth Sahib, Vadhans ki Var, salok Mahala 3, Ang 560 (ego and the Name do not dwell in one place)
Guru Granth Sahib, Ramkali Mahala 3, Anand Sahib, pauri 2, Ang 917 (O my mind, stay always with the Lord)
